chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Liusong we did not hear you either.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: you can not hear me

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: We did not hear you, Zhenqiang.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: I don't konw why

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Please note there have been some IPR declarations for some FS drafts.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: My coworker will present the first two drafts

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Understood.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: Song Liu is the psesenter

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: Ruiqian Hu is the next presenter

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The BFD WG hasn't been polled about the draft, but the mechanism shouldn't have any BFD WG specific issues.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: We can forward to the BFD WG for similar review as spring.

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: Joel - has Spring examined a requirement for the BFD feature?

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: The PCEP WG draft should have had.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: As far as I know, Spring has not discussed the question.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: We privade the same capability for SR Policy.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: How many NRPs are expected to be attached to SR policies?

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: Has srv6ops looked at the scaling issues in the split of NRP-ID?

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: I generally worry about carry ids in Ecom.. will it increase number of ecoms?

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: Also what happens if Ecoms are dropped?

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: The latest reference I can find to BFD on the spring email list is from August of 2025.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Use of BFD with SR is common. The mechanism for carrying the provisioning for the BFD sessions in the BGP state is the novel item.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: How many NRPs are expected to be attached to SR policies?--It depends on the service demands and the forwarding resource along the SR Policy path that can satisfy the requirements.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: @Jeffrey Haas, yes, the base idea is well known.   I was merely trying to find any relevant discussion which might be about this usage, and couldn't.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I presume it is deliberate that the filter dependencies are not directional.  I.e. they can express that fitler 1 and 2 are coupled, but can't express that a failure of filter 1 blocks 2, but a failure of 2 wouldn't need to block 1?

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: PCEP extension for this purpose is already a WG document in PCE WG.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text:
The reason to ask about the number of NRPs is that a large number may not fit. Each extended community uses 8 octets of the usual 4k octets available for BGP. If the list is meant to be fairly short, this is not a significant concern for PDU space.
Keyur's question about how extended communities might be filtered is still important.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: FS filters in the base spec are NOT directional, Joel.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: One service requires one NRP ID extended community when advertising its routes.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: I wwasn't asking if the fitler was directional.  Rather, I was wondering about directional dependency, e.g. 2 depends upon 1 but 1 doesn't depend upon 2.  Not coverign that case is quite reasonable.  It just struck me wathching the presentaiton.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: FS filters were at least in FSv1 implicitly always inboud

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The dependency is "all that share the same ID". They are not individually numbered with a dependency graph.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: And I was trying to confirm that the omission was deliberate.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: @Sue, Yang Huang also prepared some slides for the origin-AS/community drafts

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: Zhiwen AN

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: Doesn't the compression also need encapsulation parameters in addition to the comrpession parameters?

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: email a great way to handle it.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Joel, I think encapsulation information is also needed, while may be based on existing actions

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Note that there's an overlapping FSM discussion about maintaining the FSM as part of the bfd-strict review on IDR right now.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: If this draft wants to say "There must also be an eencapsualtion or tunneling action for the same match criteria, and put give them the same dependence ID, that can work.  Just asking for sufficiently clarity about the necessary and sufficient conditions for using the compression action.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Very necessary since inconsistent application of compression can result in the egress node getting traffic it doesn't know how to deal with.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: For the record ... I voiced concern if this should be part of base spec considering upcoming BGP over QUIC where sessions may not need to fate share the same transport connection.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Nit: BGP over QUIC is all over the same QUIC connection, but different streams. :-)

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: (but the point is relevant)

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: Thx Jeff for terminology fix

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The IESG (among others) is likely to aim a lot of hate at the non-normative nature of "discouraged".

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: I would vote to keep the draft simpler.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: instead of saying XXX is discouraged, maybe just  same YYY is recommended?

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Or maybe "preferred" to avoid overlap with RECOMMENDED. But yes, good idea.

chat.author: John Scudder
Robert Raszuk
chat.text:
IMHO RFC4760 fits much better to be integrated with 4271bis then 7606 :) 
In fact it may put separate NEXT_HOP attribute to be obsoleted for good.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text:
The place that folding 4760 in gets messy is that pushes to fold in capabilities.
I tend to be personally fond of the idea of the omnibus style to roll in all of the important things, but that's not what the current work scope suggests.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: The rubric for accepting changes into 4271bis is basically, "is it shipping, and is it baked? or is it new?"

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: If we can make the case that nh-selection is just documenting existing practice then IMO it's a good candidate for folding in. Else, not.

chat.author: Kaliraj Vairavakkalai
chat.text:
except for suggesting the new path-sel change using a new-preference it is documenting existing practice. 
The new preference itself is not mandatory IMO, since today Resolution-Schemes are able to provide same functionality without path-sel change.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text:
Olivier ... do you agree to put your forwarding address into protocol NEXT HOP field of MP_REACH or not. 
That's pretty much the only point I want to make clear so NEXT_HOP is still valid for all BGP operational reasons.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Jeff's audio is unusable for me. Is it general?

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Or just me?

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Same here

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: I'll stick to text.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: We care about 3 things:

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: You don't need to read sue. :-)

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Is the next hop reachable for forwarding purposes and can we use that as a tie breaking step in BGP?  There's a lot of support for that.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: BGP has a hidden property that's not in 4271 but should be: We require that the next hop permit route selection converge the selection of the path toward the "exit".  We still care about this even if the forwarding can be different because it's required for the protocol to select routes across the network consistently.

chat.author: Olivier Vroonen
chat.text: The next-hop reachability check is for path validation but for tie breaking as we report the metric of the resolution tuple, the next hop is not used

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The hard point is what do we do about forwarding when it's different than the property 2, above?  Especially if this may differ on a hop by hop basis.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The hard discussion is one part "picking a resolution scheme" as Kaliraj points out.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: We can not have part done against one address and the other part against the other one. Makes no sense

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: But it's also "how do you make sure this is done consistently across the domain to avoid forwarding loops due to inconsistent deployment"

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The answer is likely to be one part protocol extension, and significantly an operational consideration.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Keeping properties 2 and 3 aligned simplifies things quite a bit. But that's not how we're building things.

chat.author: Olivier Vroonen
chat.text: we can discuss the routing loop, but we have a section about it and as it's mistly for tunneling technology, intermediate nodes don't do a lookup and then minimizing the risk of routing loop

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: A note about NNHN, it biases load balancing but has no other impact.  ECMP is horribly under-standardized beyond link-bw. :-)

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Properties 2 and 3 diverging largely works out as long as we tunnel to the egress. That's the wisdom we've operated on in IDR and BESS for a while. It's not really written down anywhere.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: 4271 is written completely in terms of hop-by-hop. It may be worth scrubbing that. (Although it also may be worth not digging the 4271bis hole any deeper...)

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: For your rubric, the big headache is practice has wildly diverged from explicit documentation in RFCs.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Thus the motivation for these talks.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: As Olivier said, most of the cases described in the nh selection draft is about path selection in tunnel  based forwarding. Maybe we can consider to limit the scope of the new path selection to that?

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Determining scope of the draft is part of the discussion. The whole of the problem needs to be addressed, but in one or more than one document?

chat.author: Kaliraj Vairavakkalai
chat.text: one minor nit - on slide 9, last row. only rfc9832 talks about impact to 4271.9.1.2. I dont see anything related to this in rfc9723 or rfc9871.

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: This will break upgr

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: @kaliraj .. Your observation is not correct ... We have been distributing best and 2nd best or best external for decades

chat.author: Keyur Patel
chat.text: Update groups and be performance intensive

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: RFC6774

chat.author: Donatas Abraitis
chat.text: :ok:

chat.author: Kaliraj Vairavakkalai
chat.text: from perspective of one RR, it is one path, without addpath. And yea with 6774 in the mix, u can say today it is 1, 2 or N paths. with this new model it is 1..N per-receiver control.

chat.author: Donatas Abraitis
chat.text: Keyour, I don't get the point how this would break upgrades?

chat.author: Donatas Abraitis
chat.text: Or update-groups you meant?

chat.author: Kaliraj Vairavakkalai
chat.text: because each peer in a group may ask for a difference addpath-recv size. Yea, update-groups.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text:
@kaliraj ... Since day one of Add-paths there was ALWAYS consideration to distribute less then all paths ... Literally N paths as selected by operator on either sender or receiver. Pls see: 
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-idr-add-paths-guidelines-08

chat.author: Donatas Abraitis
chat.text: IMO, it's non-sense. Update-groups are invented for outbound optimizations, so if we have a updgrp which is quite heavy with 100 paths, then it's absoltely make sense to give that a separate update-group

chat.author: Kaliraj Vairavakkalai
chat.text: N in my comment is not all-paths. what I mean is whatever is advertise by RR those N paths are received consistently by all receivers.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: But Donatas is not changing that .. he is only signalling what operator configured

chat.author: Kaliraj Vairavakkalai
chat.text: no, it is changing that each recevier may receive different path-count. which is not the case today.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: only if operator configured so

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: The pathological case is an update group with (say) peers asking for N=5, 6, ... , 10. You take a group of 6 peers and turn it into 6 groups of 1 peer. ISTM (without checking in the draft...) that the receiver could opt to send floor(5,6,...,10) paths == 5 paths, and not break the group.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: add-paths, in its normal implementation and opertaion, already sends a wildly varying number of paths.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Move we adjourn
